content: Bedford Hospital is a District General Hospital located in Bedford, England, serving the populations of north and mid Bedfordshire. It is managed by Bedford Hospital NHS Trust. The hospital's primary site is known as the South Wing, which accommodates several key medical services. These include the Accident and Emergency (A&E) department, operating theatres, pathology services, inpatient wards, radiology (x-ray) services, oncology care, and outpatient clinics. Additionally, the South Wing is home to BEDOC, the out-of-hours emergency service provided by Bedford Primary Care Trust for general practitioner (GP) care. Several significant developments have taken place at the South Wing site in recent years: The Cygnet Wing, opened in 1996, is a dedicated facility for paediatric, maternity, and gynaecology services. A new critical care complex was established in 2002 to enhance intensive care services. The Macmillan Primrose Centre, an oncology unit funded entirely through charitable donations from the local community, was inaugurated in 2003. Beeden House, opened in 2005, includes a cardiology suite. A state-of-the-art pathology building, costing £7 million, was also completed in 2005. The South Wing houses various wards, each serving specific patient needs: Gifford Nash Ward: A medical ward for elderly female patients. John Bunyan Ward: A 16-bed ward for elderly female patients. Meadowbank Ward: A special care baby unit (SCBU) located in the Cygnet Wing, with 14 cots for neonatal care. Pilgrim Ward: Specific details not provided. Reginald Hart Ward: A 14-bed ward for female patients requiring trauma and orthopaedic care. Richard Wells Ward: A medical ward specializing in respiratory conditions. Robertson Ward: A 16-bed ward for female patients undergoing major gynaecological or breast surgery. Shand Ward: A 34-bed mixed surgical ward with a focus on vascular surgery. Shuttleworth Ward: A 33-bed mixed surgical ward specializing in colorectal and gastrointestinal surgery. Victoria Ward: A 16-bed ward dedicated to stroke patients. The North Wing of Bedford Hospital, located approximately two miles from the South Wing, provides additional services. These include occupational therapy, physiotherapy, rehabilitation facilities, a chest clinic, and a drop-in dental service. Historically, the North Wing housed the hospital's maternity ward, but this was relocated to the Cygnet Wing at the South Wing in 1996. Psychiatric services for the area are primarily delivered at the Weller Wing, which is also located on the South Wing site. However, these services are managed by a separate organization, the Bedfordshire and Luton Mental Health and Social Care Partnership NHS Trust. The Weller Wing includes the following wards: Keats Ward: A 24-bed unit for acute adult psychiatric care. Brontë Ward: An 18-bed unit for acute adult psychiatric care. Chaucer Ward: A 15-bed unit specializing in old-age psychiatry. Milton Ward: A 15-bed unit focusing on dementia and other organic psychiatric illnesses in older adults. Sheridan Day Hospital: A day hospital providing care for up to 15 individuals aged 65 and older. In 2001, Bedford Hospital faced a significant controversy involving its mortuary services. During maintenance work on part of the mortuary, bodies were inappropriately stored on the floor of the chapel of rest. This issue was exposed in local and national media, with photographs of the deceased being published, causing distress to the families involved. An inquiry determined that the hospital's management was at fault, leading to the resignation of the Chief Executive. Temporary refrigerated trucks were used as makeshift mortuaries for several months to prevent further incidents. The issue has since been resolved, with the new pathology building now housing an expanded and modern mortuary facility.
